title: Developer Fidelity Mosaic — Playbook for Developer Onboarding and Fidelity Choices
summary: This playbook describes the Developer Fidelity Mosaic: a product- and operations-focused playbook that helps engineering teams adopt and tune Redwood's fidelity surface (developer presets, fidelity negotiation APIs, and telemetry hooks) to match application needs. It bundles onboarding steps, default SLOs and thresholds, UX patterns, rollout recommendations, and post-onboarding diagnostics for both self-serve and sales-assisted customers.
audience: Product managers and PMMs defining developer-facing fidelity options
SDK and frontend engineers building onboarding UX and presets
Solutions and customer success engineers running onboarding and migrations
Reliability and observability teams that instrument fidelity telemetry
goals: 1. Reduce time-to-value for developers by providing opinionated fidelity presets that map to common latency/cost/quality tradeoffs.
2. Enable predictable migrations from hosted -> dedicated -> private by codifying fidelity contracts and telemetry signals.
3. Provide a standardized instrumentation surface so Optimize and Console can auto-recommend fidelity adjustments.
problem-statement: Teams face repeated friction: developers cannot map product needs to fidelity settings, fidelity experiments are noisy, and migrations leak cost/latency surprises. The Mosaic playbook standardizes presets, evaluation criteria, and rollout mechanics so customers experience predictable economics and controlled quality changes.
components: Fidelity Preset Library: curated presets (fast-approx, balanced, high-precision) with explicit token/latency/cost expectations.
Developer Preflight Assistant: a lightweight SDK/CLI that runs workload probes and recommends a preset.
Fidelity Negotiation API: runtime endpoint that allows clients to supply a fidelity budget and receive negotiated responses (with fallback headers).
Observability Signals: standardized telemetry schema for fidelity events, regressions, and cost-delta attribution.
Onboarding Playbooks: step-by-step runbooks for self-serve and sales-assisted workflows.
onboarding-workflows:
Self-serve (recommended for SMB / Developer teams):
1. Developer signs up and receives the Developer Preflight CLI in Console -> Developer Tools.
2. Run `redwood preflight --preset balanced --samples 50` to collect latency/cost/quality fingerprints.
3. Preflight outputs recommended preset (+ tolerances) and a one-click apply link for Sandbox routes.
4. Developer integrates the SDK preset and enables telemetry reporting (opt-in) so Optimize can recommend future adjustments.

Sales-assisted enterprise onboarding (for Dedicated/Private):
1. Solutions engineer runs a controlled benchmark using the Tenant Fidelity Emulation harness (10k synthetic requests across workload shapes).
2. Joint review session with customer to select baseline fidelity preset and define SLOs (latency p50/p95, token cost target).
3. Apply fidelity contract via Contract Orchestrator; configure rollouts to ramp 5% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days with regression gates.
4. Post-migration retrospective using the Fidelity Regression Report template.
success-metrics: Time-to-first-stable-preset: target < 3 business days for sales-assisted, < 4 hours for self-serve.
Fidelity-to-cost mapping error: median predicted vs observed token cost delta < 8% after 30K tokens.
Regression rate: fidelity-related quality regressions during rollouts < 1% of requests.
defaults-and-slos-table:
| preset name | expected p50 latency | expected p95 latency | estimated token multiplier | default SLOs |
|-------------|---------------------:|---------------------:|---------------------------:|------------|
| fast-approx  | 50 ms               | 200 ms               | 0.85                      | p95 < 250ms, cost target < baseline *0.9 |
| balanced     | 120 ms              | 400 ms               | 1.00                      | p95 < 500ms, cost target = baseline |
| high-precision | 250 ms            | 900 ms               | 1.45                      | p95 < 1s, quality delta < 0.5% |
fidelity-telemetry-spec: event.fidelity.applied: emitted when a preset is applied (fields: tenant_id, route, preset_name, src)
event.fidelity.decision: emitted at runtime negotiation (fields: input_budget_tokens, negotiated_preset, fallback_used)
metric.fidelity.cost_delta: percent change vs baseline cost per 1k tokens
alert.fidelity.regression: triggers when model-quality check fails on regression prompts (> threshold)
rollout-and-guardrails: Canary staging: 0% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automated rollback on fidelity.regression alerts.
Regression gates: fail rollout if A/B shadow evals show >0.75% degradation on prioritized prompt set.
Cost guard: if observed cost multiplier exceeds expected by 15% for >1 hour, pause rollout and notify customer.
migration-playbook:
Use-case: migrating a tenant from hosted balanced preset to Dedicated high-precision for mission-critical throughput.
Steps:
1. Baseline capture: collect 72h of traffic traces and preflight probe results.
2. Capacity mapping: estimate required Dedicated GPU pool using the Serving Cost Estimator (attach table for required GPUs and expected tokens/sec).
3. Contract and entitlement: create entitlement in Contract Orchestrator and agree on SLO crediting.
4. Staged rollout: use the rollout-and-guardrails above with extended ramp (7–14 days) and manual check-ins at 20% and 60%.
5. Post-migration: run fidelity regression report and cost-reconciliation; create a change request if drift >10%.
ownership-and-roles: Product: owns the Fidelity Preset Library and product UX for preflight assistant.
Engineering (SDK): owns Developer Preflight Assistant and Fidelity Negotiation API.
Eng-Platform/Optimize: owns telemetry collection, recommendation pipeline, and cost simulations.
Solutions / CSE: responsible for sales-assisted benchmarks and migration coordination.
risks-and-mitigations: Risk: noisy preflight results due to cold-start variance. Mitigation: require minimum 500 tokens and 3 distinct workload shapes per probe.
Risk: customer confusion about terms (preset vs negotiated fidelity). Mitigation: developer docs and in-Console explainer with example graphs.
Risk: cost creep during private deployment. Mitigation: conservative default token multipliers and pre-migration capacity simulation.
rollout-roadmap:
Q2 2026: Launch Developer Preflight CLI + three initial presets (fast-approx, balanced, high-precision).
Q3 2026: Integrate with Optimize recommendations and Console one-click apply for Sandbox routes.
Q4 2026: Fidelity Negotiation API v1 and telemetry schema GA; begin enterprise migrations pilot.
title_meta: Developer Fidelity Mosaic — Playbook for Developer Onboarding and Fidelity Choices
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose
-------
This document is a prescriptive playbook for enabling developer teams to choose and operationalize fidelity settings that balance latency, cost, and output quality. It is intended to be actionable: each section contains concrete steps, configuration defaults, ownership, and rollback criteria.

Quick start
-----------
- Self-serve: Console -> Developer Tools -> Run the Preflight CLI and apply the recommended preset to a Sandbox route.
- Sales-assisted: Request Solutions engineering benchmark and adopt the staged rollout with regression gates described below.

Diagnostics and postmortem checklist
-----------------------------------
1. Verify telemetry: event.fidelity.* events are present for affected routes.
2. Re-run preflight with same workload shapes; compare cost_delta and latency distributions.
3. If regression detected, capture 200 failing examples and run the shadow-eval harness.

Appendix: example CLI output
---------------------------
$ redwood preflight --preset balanced --samples 100
Recommended preset: balanced
Observed p50: 110ms, p95: 420ms
Estimated token multiplier: 1.03
Suggested action: apply preset to /api/chat-sandbox and monitor fidelity.cost_delta < 12% for 24h
